# A computable four-color partition from a public primitive Gaussian norm

Status: proof plus bounded actual typed BRC execution; shared-context author contribution, not independently admitted. Current EM snapshot: `e8c5726a22d78c8d3623611afd33f4fe76b46321`. Activity: `RA-CAAAC604CB513AEA8BBC1DFC`. The current GK arithmetic constraint and machine mirror were read at `f44ed5959c92e6e088c61c102951d1ab2c5e98d4` before execution. P000, phase precision, native dynamics and complete residual carriers are unchanged.

## 1. Result and its distinction from the previous certificate

Given public nonzero integers `u,v` of opposite parity with `gcd(u,v)=1` and `N=u^2+v^2 >= 3`, there is an explicitly implemented character

\[
 C:(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^*\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z
\]

such that, for rational integer work labels,

\[
 C(xy\bmod N)=C(x)+C(y)\bmod4,\qquad
 (-1)^{C(w)}=J(w,N).
\]

`color_trace(w, certificate)` computes this color directly from `w,u,v`; it does not need a latent path exponent, factorization, order, work-support enumeration, or a discrete logarithm. Nonunits return a zero symbol and **no color**. A negative Jacobi symbol of the program base makes `C(a)` odd and therefore gives a surjective four-color character on the cyclic orbit generated by `a`.

The preceding power-sum certificate already established a two-bit suffix on this input family through order divisibility. The new result supplies an actual **bare-work-label query** and quantitative color-mass overlap bounds. It does not claim a new family-wide factoring speedup merely by reproving the same two-bit suffix.

## 2. Definition, denominator conditions and square law

Write `pi=u+iv` and use its principal ideal as the denominator. For an odd Gaussian prime ideal `P`, the quartic symbol is the unique element of `{0,1,i,-1,-i}` whose reduction is `alpha^((Norm(P)-1)/4)`. Extend by multiplying over prime ideal factors with multiplicity. The unit ideal has symbol one. This definition, primary convention and the reciprocity formulas used below are given in [Bach and Sandlund, *On Euclidean Methods for Cubic and Quartic Jacobi Symbols*, section 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.07719#page=13). Their displayed sentence on rational-prime splitting contains a typographical duplication of `1 mod 4`; the correct inert class is `3 mod 4`, as also follows directly from whether `-1` is a square in the rational prime field. No conclusion here uses that typo.

Define `chi(w)=(w/(pi))_4=i^C(w)` on rational units. An odd norm excludes the ramified ideal `(1+i)`. If `p | N` and `p=3 mod 4`, then `p | u^2+v^2` forces `p | u,v`, contradicting primitiveness. Likewise both conjugate ideals over a split prime cannot divide `pi`, since their product is `(p)` and would divide both coordinates. Thus each rational prime `p | N` occurs in exactly one orientation of split Gaussian prime ideals; its norm is `p`, with the same multiplicity as in `N`.

At this prime ideal, squaring the defining fourth-power character gives the ordinary quadratic character of the rational residue modulo `p`. Multiplying with multiplicities proves

\[
 \chi(w)^2=\prod_{p^e\parallel N}(w/p)^e=J(w,N).
\]

This is an identity for a composite denominator, not a prime-only Euler shortcut. It remains correct at nonunits because both sides are zero. The Jacobi product convention is described in [NIST DLMF 27.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.9).

Multiplicativity follows prime ideal by prime ideal. Because `N=pi*conjugate(pi)` lies in the denominator ideal, replacing an integer by its residue modulo `N` leaves the symbol unchanged. This proves the advertised transport law for actual modular permutations. Replacing the denominator by any unit associate leaves its ideal and the symbol unchanged. Conjugating the denominator conjugates the rational-label symbol, reversing the color orientation; the opposite orientation is still a valid character.

The square identity in fact extends to every odd Gaussian norm, although the public `certify_character` interface deliberately retains the primitive condition. Inert factors then have norm `p^2`; the quadratic character of a rational nonzero element in the field of size `p^2` is one, matching the even exponent in the integer norm. If both split orientations occur, their multiplicities add. This extension is a mathematical observation, not a relaxation of the implemented character certificate.

## 3. Actual Euclidean algorithm and the signs that matter

The symbol observer accepts any Gaussian numerator and any nonzero odd Gaussian denominator. A Gaussian integer `c+di` is primary exactly when `d` is even and `c+d=1 mod 4`. Every odd Gaussian integer has exactly one primary unit associate. The observer normalizes the denominator without a numerator correction because the denominator is an ideal.

For current primary denominator `beta=c+di`, form an exact nearest-coordinate Gaussian quotient and remainder

\[
 \alpha=q\beta+\gamma,\qquad
 \operatorname{Norm}(\gamma)\le\operatorname{Norm}(\beta)/2.
\]

Ties are rounded away from zero independently in the two coordinates. The remainder bound follows since each coordinate of the quotient error is at most one half. The implementation also checks the bound with typed arithmetic. If the nonunit divisor has zero remainder the symbol is zero. A unit denominator terminates with one.

Otherwise extract all factors `lambda=1+i`, then divide by one of the four units to obtain

\[
 \gamma=(1+i)^m i^j\delta,\qquad \delta=e+fi\text{ primary},\quad 0\le j<4.
\]

The exact division by `1+i` sends `(x,y)` to `((x+y)/2,(y-x)/2)` and is integral exactly when the two coordinates have the same parity. This handles even numerators; even denominators are rejected. Set

\[
 H=(c-d-d^2-1)/4,\quad B=(c-1)/2,\quad A=(e-1)/2.
\]

The two supplements and reciprocity give the recursion

\[
 (\alpha/\beta)_4=i^{\,mH-jB+2AB}(\beta/\delta)_4.
\]

All three displayed divisions are integral under the primary conditions. The observer accumulates the exponent modulo four, then replaces the ordered pair by `(beta,delta)`. Numerator units are accounted for by `-jB`; omitting that term or treating numerator and denominator unit normalization identically would be incorrect. The reciprocity term `2AB` is also retained for composite denominators. When numerator and denominator are not coprime, both reciprocal symbols vanish and the eventual nonunit gcd termination returns zero.

This is a scalar arithmetic observer of an existing number-theoretic function. Gaussian pairs do not encode evolving state amplitudes, and the root-of-unity labels `i^k` are never applied as a replacement native propagator. The proof and implementation require no floating point, trigonometric function, ideal QFT dynamics or increased phase precision.

## 4. Why the typed implementation has polynomial cost

`SignedGaussian` represents signed integer labels using a sign and an unsigned magnitude. Signs, unit rotations, coordinate permutations and loop counters are declared host wiring. Positive magnitude addition, subtraction/comparison, multiplication, exact division, nearest-quotient decisions and nonnegative residues are all compositions of the frozen actual BRC full-adder transducer. Each operation retains a pointer to its underlying trace; two's-complement differences are used only with the appropriate sign/magnitude case. Native kernel calls, full-adder digit replays and host wiring have distinct counters.

Each remainder stage at least halves the denominator norm; extracting `1+i` only reduces it further. Thus there are `O(log Norm(beta))` stages. For inputs with `n` bits of coordinate/norm size, exact schoolbook multiplication and division use `O(n^2)` typed digit work per stage and the conservative total is `O(n^3)`, with polynomial trace size. The sum of ramified-factor extractions is also `O(n)`, since every extraction divides the norm by two. No potentially exponential even-quotient algorithm is used. We have not implemented the approximate-quotient optimization needed for a sharper bit bound.

`color_trace` currently rebuilds the public character certificate on each query. That conservative validation work, including typed gcd and norm checks, is additional polynomial work. It is not counted as a free lookup. Discovering a useful public norm representation for an arbitrary modulus remains an independent problem.

## 5. Exact suffix and quantitative near separation

For the canonical actual reverse-square schedule starting at work label one, rounds before the last two multiply by powers `a^(multiple of 4)`. Their character shift is zero. If `C(a)` is odd, all reachable work labels therefore have color zero before the penultimate round. Its multiplier `a^2` has color two, so the unshifted and shifted supports are disjoint. The next parent is supported on colors `{0,2}`; the final shift by odd `C(a)` lands on `{1,3}`. Every reachable positive-mass history has both disjointness properties.

For a complete raw parent field `v`, write `M=sum_w ||v_w||^2`. The actual branch rows are `(v_z+sigma*T v_(P^-1 z))/2`. On either of these disjoint-support rounds, their joint outcome/label law is

\[
 \Pr(\sigma,z\mid h)=
 \frac{\|v_z\|^2+\|v_{P^{-1}z}\|^2}{4M}.
\]

A fair choice between latent `W` and `PW`, followed by an independent fair reported bit, samples this joint law. Its latent invariant is renewed, so the two consecutive bits can both omit their scoring row queries. This conclusion keeps the complete history and original row oracle for any future field reconstruction. It accepts no arbitrary initial or midrun state; the existing full program binding is preserved. Internal isometries may be history dependent and need not commute with those at other rounds. They preserve work labels and all 61 internal coordinates.

For a general parent supported on unit work labels (as in the canonical program), normalize color masses by

\[
 p_c=M^{-1}\sum_{C(w)=c}\|v_w\|^2,
 \qquad d=C(P).
\]

With the complete internal isometry retained, Cauchy-Schwarz separately in each color gives the non-asymptotic certificate

\[
 |\kappa_h|:=\left|\operatorname{Re}\langle v,TPv\rangle/M\right|
 \le \sum_{c\in\mathbb Z/4}\sqrt{p_c p_{c-d}}.
\]

This upper-bounds the absolute signed interference, including every residual component. The reported-bit law differs from a fair coin by at most half the displayed bound in total variation.

For the joint reported-bit/latent-label law, signed cancellation across labels is insufficient. Define the stronger quantity

\[
 L_h=\sum_z|\langle v_z,Tv_{P^{-1}z}\rangle|.
\]

The same colorwise Cauchy-Schwarz argument, now after taking each label's absolute value, gives

\[
 L_h/M\le\sum_c\sqrt{p_c p_{c-d}}.
\]

In the actual real native representation, retaining the fair proposal `W` or `PW` but replacing the local outcome by a fair coin has one-step **joint** total-variation cost exactly `L_h/(2M)`, averaged over the exact conditional parent latent law. Indeed, at each label the two outcome-mass errors are the opposite values `+/-<v_z,Tv_(P^-1 z)>/(2M)`. For a complex representation the same bound holds with the real parts in the exact error and the displayed absolute inner product as an upper bound. This is the current general partition theorem specialized to this computable quartic character. The weaker signed quantity `kappa_h` only controls the reported-bit marginal; it is not substituted for `L_h` in a joint sampler estimate. Multiple approximate rounds still require the joint reference-kernel telescoping argument and the retained full history/oracle.

If a set of colors `A` satisfies `A` disjoint from `A+d`, and the parent mass outside `A` is `e <= epsilon <= 1/2`, the shifted mass in `A` is at most `e`. Coarsening into `A` and its complement and applying Cauchy-Schwarz yields

\[
 |\kappa_h|\le2\sqrt{e(1-e)}\le2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}.
\]

For the middle inequality, with fixed `e <= 1/2`, the binary overlap `sqrt((1-e)x)+sqrt(e(1-x))` is increasing for `0 <= x <= e`, so its maximum on that interval is attained at `x=e`. This same bound applies to `L_h/M`, so both the reported-bit bias and the one-step fair-replacement joint cost are at most `sqrt(epsilon(1-epsilon))`.

These are bounds conditional on an established parent color-mass bound. A cheap label character does not, by itself, give all four masses or certify a rare-prefix leakage bound. An exact latent sample supplies one unbiased color observation; arbitrary independent samples conditioned on a fixed history are not granted for free. When `d=0`, the color overlap bound is one and can be useless. In the original square schedule this four-color character has zero shift before the last two rounds, so it alone cannot remove the growing central coherent block.

More generally, merging work labels into color classes can only increase the classical overlap bound: by Cauchy-Schwarz, `sum_w sqrt(p_w q_w) <= sum_c sqrt(p_c q_c)`. Thus when even the full singleton-label mass overlap is near one, a four-color bound cannot certify small interference. This does not prove actual signed interference is large; phase cancellation may still matter. It explains why this partition does not solve the general middle-round coherence problem.

## 6. Bounded execution evidence

`check_typed_quartic.py` completed with the following results:

- 35 rational-numerator prime-field cases at norms 5, 13 and 17 matched the defining Euler character, with both modular powers and the image of `i` computed using actual typed BRC arithmetic;
- 12 general Gaussian cases exercised negative/even/complex numerators, unit denominators, nonunit zero symbols, inert and composite denominators;
- all 175 residues across `N=25,65,85` satisfied the square law against the frozen actual Jacobi observer, and complete multiplication-by-base transport was checked on those same residue sets;
- 10 cases matched a composite-denominator product via the explicitly verified fixture `(−1+2i)(3−2i)=1+8i`; these known factors are isolated definition-test data, not inputs to the generic algorithm;
- two full actual `t=4` programs, `N=65,a=3` and `N=85,a=2`, supplied 23 positive prefixes and 36 certified fair terminal child edges; all computed bare-label colors showed the required support separation, complete 61-component fields were retained, and terminal mass was exactly one;
- ten negative controls rejected malformed denominators, false/nonprimitive norm witnesses, altered colors/source/boundaries and an injected initial field; a non-certifying base retained `UNAVAILABLE`.

The complete fixture made 244 native core calls. The symbol-only full-adder digit cost ranged from 196 to 1,074 at `N=25`, 161 to 1,284 at `N=65`, and 250 to 1,844 at `N=85`. Each color query additionally replays the norm certificate: respectively 104/71/130 digit operations plus gcd costs 44/26/52. These per-certificate counters do not pretend to be a global runtime total. Full traces, source bindings and native-call receipts are retained in the payload.

The implementation is a concrete polynomial-cost label query on a supplied arithmetic family. The small checks validate this implementation and the native binding; they do not establish generic Shor dequantization, a speed advantage over classical structured factoring, or a new physical residual attribution.

The classical comparison must receive the same witness. Primitiveness and `N=u^2+v^2` imply every prime divisor is `1 mod 4`; trial division can restrict candidates to that class. This only gives a constant-factor candidate reduction at order four, but it is still useful classical information and cannot be withheld from the comparator. A second appropriately different norm representation may itself yield a gcd split, so representation discovery and any additional structure must also be charged. The present implementation does not benchmark or claim superiority over such methods. Its contribution is the executable label character and exact transport/overlap certificate, not an additional suffix length beyond the already certified two bits.
